raw: CHAPTER XX. A Plea
en: [Chapter 20] A Plea

raw: When the newly-married pair came home, the first person who appeared, to offer his congratulations, was Sydney Carton.
en: When the newly married couple returned home, the first person to offer his congratulations was Sydney Carton.
ko: 신혼부부가 집으로 돌아왔을 때, 가장 먼저 축하 인사를 건넨 사람은 시드니 카턴이었다.

raw: They had not been at home many hours, when he presented himself.
en: They had been home for only a few hours when he arrived.
ko: 그가 도착했을 때 그들이 집에 온 지는 불과 몇 시간밖에 되지 않았다.

raw: He was not improved in habits, or in looks, or in manner; but there was a certain rugged air of fidelity about him, which was new to the observation of Charles Darnay.
en: He had not improved in his habits, appearance, or manners, but Charles Darnay noticed a new, rugged look of loyalty in him.
ko: 그는 습관, 외모, 또는 태도에서 전혀 나아지지 않았지만, 찰스 다네이는 그에게서 새롭고 억센 충성심의 모습을 발견했다.

raw: He watched his opportunity of taking Darnay aside into a window, and of speaking to him when no one overheard.
en: Carton waited for an opportunity to take Darnay aside by the window, where no one else could hear them speak.
ko: 카턴은 아무도 그들의 대화를 들을 수 없는 창가로 다네이를 따로 데려갈 기회를 기다렸다.

raw: “Mr.
en: Carton said, "Mr.
ko: 카턴이 말했다. "미스터

raw: Darnay,” said Carton, “I wish we might be friends.”
en: Darnay, I wish we might be friends."
ko: 다네이, 우리가 친구가 될 수 있기를 바랍니다."

raw: “We are already friends, I hope.”
en: "We are already friends, I hope."
ko: "우리는 이미 친구이기를 바랍니다."

raw: “You are good enough to say so, as a fashion of speech; but, I don’t mean any fashion of speech.
en: "You are polite enough to say so as a formality, but I don't mean it as a mere formality.
ko: "당신은 형식적으로 그렇게 말할 만큼 정중하지만, 저는 그것을 단순한 형식적인 의미로 말하는 것이 아닙니다.

raw: Indeed, when I say I wish we might be friends, I scarcely mean quite that, either.”
en: Indeed, when I say I wish we might be friends, I don't even mean exactly that, either."
ko: 사실, 제가 우리가 친구가 될 수 있기를 바란다고 말할 때, 저 역시 정확히 그런 의미를 뜻하는 것도 아닙니다."

raw: Charles Darnay--as was natural--asked him, in all good-humour and good-fellowship, what he did mean?
en: Charles Darnay naturally asked him, in a friendly and good-natured way, what he did mean.
ko: 찰스 다네이는 자연스럽게 그에게 다정하고 상냥한 태도로, 그가 무슨 뜻으로 한 말인지 물었다.

raw: “Upon my life,” said Carton, smiling, “I find that easier to comprehend in my own mind, than to convey to yours.
en: Carton said with a smile, "Honestly, I find that easier to understand in my own mind than to explain to you.
ko: 카턴은 미소를 지으며 말했다. "솔직히, 저는 그것을 당신에게 설명하는 것보다 제 마음속에서 이해하는 것이 더 쉽다고 생각합니다.

raw: However, let me try.
en: But let me try.
ko: 하지만 노력해 보겠습니다.

raw: You remember a certain famous occasion when I was more drunk than--than usual?”
en: You remember a certain occasion when I was more drunk than usual?"
ko: 제가 평소보다 더 취해 있었던 특정 경우를 기억하십니까?"

raw: “I remember a certain famous occasion when you forced me to confess that you had been drinking.”
en: "I remember an occasion when you made me admit you had been drinking."
ko: "당신이 술을 마셨다는 것을 저에게 인정하게 했던 때가 기억납니다."

raw: “I remember it too.
en: "I remember it too.
ko: "저도 그것을 기억합니다.

raw: The curse of those occasions is heavy upon me, for I always remember them.
en: The regret of those moments weighs heavily on me, because I always remember them.
ko: 그 순간들에 대한 후회는 저를 짓누르는데, 제가 항상 그것들을 기억하기 때문입니다.

raw: I hope it may be taken into account one day, when all days are at an end for me!
en: I hope that will be taken into account one day when my life is over!
ko: 제 삶이 끝나는 어느 날 그것이 고려되기를 바랍니다!

raw: Don’t be alarmed; I am not going to preach.”
en: Don't worry; I'm not going to give you a sermon."
ko: 걱정하지 마십시오. 당신에게 설교를 하려는 것은 아닙니다."

raw: “I am not at all alarmed.
en: "I am not worried at all.
ko: "전혀 걱정하지 않습니다.

raw: Earnestness in you, is anything but alarming to me.”
en: Sincerity in you is not alarming to me."
ko: 당신의 진심은 저를 놀라게 하지 않습니다."

raw: “Ah!” said Carton, with a careless wave of his hand, as if he waved that away. “On the drunken occasion in question (one of a large number, as you know), I was insufferable about liking you, and not liking you.
en: "Ah!" Carton said, waving his hand as if dismissing the thought. "On that occasion, one of many, as you know, I was obnoxious about whether I liked you or not.
ko: "아!" 카턴은 마치 생각을 떨쳐버리려는 듯 손을 내저으며 말했다. "아시다시피 많은 경우 중 하나였던 그 때, 저는 제가 당신을 좋아하는지 아닌지에 대해 불쾌하게 굴었습니다.

raw: I wish you would forget it.”
en: I wish you would forget it."
ko: 당신이 그것을 잊어주셨으면 합니다."

raw: “I forgot it long ago.”
en: "I forgot it long ago."
ko: "오래 전에 잊었습니다."

raw: “Fashion of speech again!
en: "Another polite formality!
ko: "또 다른 정중한 형식이군요!

raw: But, Mr.
en: But, Mr.
ko: 하지만, 미스터

raw: Darnay, oblivion is not so easy to me, as you represent it to be to you.
en: Darnay, forgetting is not as easy for me as you say it is for you.
ko: 다네이, 당신이 말하는 것처럼 잊는 것이 저에게는 쉽지 않습니다.

raw: I have by no means forgotten it, and a light answer does not help me to forget it.”
en: I haven't forgotten it, and a casual reply doesn't help me forget."
ko: 저는 그것을 잊지 않았고, 가벼운 대답은 제가 잊는 데 도움이 되지 않습니다."

raw: “If it was a light answer,” returned Darnay, “I beg your forgiveness for it.
en: Darnay said, "If it was a casual reply, I ask your forgiveness.
ko: 다네이가 말했다. "만약 그것이 가벼운 대답이었다면, 당신의 용서를 구합니다.

raw: I had no other object than to turn a slight thing, which, to my surprise, seems to trouble you too much, aside.
en: I only wanted to dismiss a minor thing that seems to worry you too much.
ko: 저는 단지 당신을 너무 걱정하게 만드는 것 같은 사소한 일을 떨쳐버리고 싶었을 뿐입니다.

raw: I declare to you, on the faith of a gentleman, that I have long dismissed it from my mind.
en: I assure you, on my honor as a gentleman, that I have forgotten it.
ko: 신사로서의 제 명예를 걸고, 저는 그것을 잊었다고 확언합니다.

raw: Good Heaven, what was there to dismiss! Have I had nothing more important to remember, in the great service you rendered me that day?”
en: And really, what was there to dismiss compared to the great help you gave me that day?"
ko: 그리고 정말이지, 당신이 그날 저에게 주신 큰 도움에 비하면 떨쳐버릴 것이 무엇이 있었겠습니까?"

raw: “As to the great service,” said Carton, “I am bound to avow to you, when you speak of it in that way, that it was mere professional claptrap, I don’t know that I cared what became of you, when I rendered it.--Mind!
en: Carton said, "As for that help, I must admit that it was just professional legal showmanship. I don't know that I cared what happened to you when I did it.
ko: 카턴이 말했다. "그 도움에 관해서라면, 그것은 단지 전문적인 법률적 쇼맨십이었음을 인정해야겠습니다. 제가 그것을 할 때 당신에게 무슨 일이 일어나는지 신경 썼는지 모르겠습니다.

raw: I say when I rendered it; I am speaking of the past.”
en: Remember, I am speaking of the past."
ko: 기억하십시오, 저는 과거에 대해 이야기하고 있습니다."

raw: “You make light of the obligation,” returned Darnay, “but I will not quarrel with _your_ light answer.”
en: Darnay replied, "You make light of the favor, but I won't argue with your reply."
ko: 다네이가 대답했다. "당신은 그 호의를 가볍게 여기시지만, 저는 당신의 대답에 논쟁하지 않겠습니다."

raw: “Genuine truth, Mr.
en: "It's the absolute truth, Mr.
ko: "이것은 절대적인 진실입니다, 미스터

raw: Darnay, trust me!
en: Darnay, believe me!
ko: 다네이, 저를 믿어주십시오!

raw: I have gone aside from my purpose; I was speaking about our being friends.
en: But I have wandered from my point; I was speaking of our friendship.
ko: 하지만 제가 요점에서 벗어났군요. 저는 우리의 우정에 대해 말하고 있었습니다.

raw: Now, you know me; you know I am incapable of all the higher and better flights of men.
en: You know me; you know I am incapable of the better qualities of men.
ko: 당신은 저를 압니다. 당신은 제가 사람들의 더 나은 자질들을 가질 능력이 없다는 것을 아십니다.

raw: If you doubt it, ask Stryver, and he’ll tell you so.”
en: If you doubt it, ask Stryver, and he’ll tell you so."
ko: 만약 당신이 그것을 의심한다면, 스트라이버에게 물어보십시오, 그러면 그가 당신에게 그렇게 말해줄 것입니다."

raw: “I prefer to form my own opinion, without the aid of his.”
en: "I prefer to form my own opinion, without his help."
ko: "저는 그의 도움 없이 제 자신의 의견을 형성하는 것을 선호합니다."

raw: “Well!
en: "Well!
ko: "글쎄요!

raw: At any rate you know me as a dissolute dog, who has never done any good, and never will.”
en: At any rate, you know me as a ruined man who has never done any good, and never will."
ko: 어쨌든, 당신은 저를 단 한 번도 좋은 일을 해본 적이 없고, 앞으로도 절대 하지 않을 망가진 사람으로 알고 계십니다."

raw: “I don’t know that you ‘never will.’”
en: "I don't know that you 'never will.'"
ko: "당신이 '앞으로도 절대 하지 않을' 것인지는 모르겠습니다."

raw: “But I do, and you must take my word for it.
en: "But I do, and you must take my word for it.
ko: "하지만 저는 알고 있고, 당신은 제 말을 믿으셔야 합니다.

raw: Well!
en: Well!
ko: 글쎄요!

raw: If you could endure to have such a worthless fellow, and a fellow of such indifferent reputation, coming and going at odd times, I should ask that I might be permitted to come and go as a privileged person here; that I might be regarded as an useless (and I would add, if it were not for the resemblance I detected between you and me, an unornamental) piece of furniture, tolerated for its old service, and taken no notice of.
en: If you can stand having such a worthless guy with a questionable reputation dropping by at random times, I'd like to ask for permission to come and go freely as a privileged guest here. I'd like to be treated like a useless piece of furniture (and I'd say an ugly one, if it weren't for the resemblance I noticed between you and me) that you just keep around out of habit and otherwise completely ignore.
ko: 만약 당신이 무작위로 들르는 의심스러운 평판을 가진 그런 쓸모없는 녀석을 견딜 수 있다면, 저는 이곳에서 특권 있는 손님으로서 자유롭게 드나들 수 있는 허락을 요청하고 싶습니다. 저는 당신이 그저 습관적으로 곁에 두고 그 외에는 완전히 무시하는 쓸모없는 가구처럼 (그리고 제가 당신과 나 사이에서 알아차린 유사성이 없었다면 못생긴 가구라고 말했을 것입니다) 취급받고 싶습니다.

raw: I doubt if I should abuse the permission.
en: I would be like a useless piece of furniture, tolerated for past services and ignored.
ko: 저는 과거의 봉사 때문에 용인되고 무시되는, 쓸모없는 가구 같을 것입니다.

raw: It is a hundred to one if I should avail myself of it four times in a year.
en: I doubt I would abuse the privilege; I probably wouldn't visit more than four times a year.
ko: 제가 그 특권을 남용할지는 의문입니다. 아마 일 년에 네 번 이상 방문하지는 않을 것입니다.

raw: It would satisfy me, I dare say, to know that I had it.”
en: It would simply comfort me to know I had the permission."
ko: 단지 제게 허락이 있다는 것을 아는 것만으로도 위로가 될 것입니다."

raw: “Will you try?”
en: "Will you try?"
ko: "노력해 보시겠습니까?"

raw: “That is another way of saying that I am placed on the footing I have indicated.
en: "That means I am accepted on those terms.
ko: "그것은 제가 그런 조건으로 받아들여졌다는 뜻이군요.

raw: I thank you, Darnay.
en: Thank you, Darnay.
ko: 감사합니다, 다네이.

raw: I may use that freedom with your name?”
en: May I use your first name?"
ko: 이름을 불러도 되겠습니까?"

raw: “I think so, Carton, by this time.”
en: "I think so, Carton, by this time."
ko: "그럴 때도 된 것 같군요, 카턴."

raw: They shook hands upon it, and Sydney turned away.
en: They shook hands, and Sydney turned away.
ko: 그들은 악수를 나누었고, 시드니는 돌아섰다.

raw: Within a minute afterwards, he was, to all outward appearance, as unsubstantial as ever.
en: Within a minute, he returned to his usual careless manner.
ko: 일 분 안에 그는 평소의 부주의한 태도로 돌아갔다.

raw: When he was gone, and in the course of an evening passed with Miss Pross, the Doctor, and Mr.
en: When he was gone, during an evening spent with Miss Pross, the Doctor, and Mr.
ko: 그가 떠난 후, 프로스 양, 박사, 그리고 미스터

raw: Lorry, Charles Darnay made some mention of this conversation in general terms, and spoke of Sydney Carton as a problem of carelessness and recklessness.
en: Lorry, Charles Darnay mentioned this talk. He described Sydney Carton as a puzzle of carelessness and irresponsibility.
ko: 로리와 함께 보낸 저녁 시간에 찰스 다네이는 이 대화를 언급했다. 그는 시드니 카턴을 부주의와 무책임의 미스터리라고 묘사했다.

raw: He spoke of him, in short, not bitterly or meaning to bear hard upon him, but as anybody might who saw him as he showed himself.
en: He did not speak bitterly, but simply as anyone would who saw Carton as he presented himself.
ko: 그는 씁쓸하게 말하지 않고, 단지 카턴이 자신을 나타내는 모습을 본 사람이라면 누구나 그럴 것처럼 단순하게 말했다.

raw: He had no idea that this could dwell in the thoughts of his fair young wife; but, when he afterwards joined her in their own rooms, he found her waiting for him with the old pretty lifting of the forehead strongly marked.
en: He had no idea that his young wife was thinking deeply about this. But when he joined her in their room later, he found her waiting for him with a serious look on her face.
ko: 그는 그의 젊은 아내가 이것에 대해 깊이 생각하고 있다는 것을 전혀 알지 못했다. 그러나 나중에 그가 그들의 방에서 그녀와 합류했을 때, 그는 그녀가 심각한 표정으로 그를 기다리고 있는 것을 발견했다.

raw: “We are thoughtful to-night!” said Darnay, drawing his arm about her.
en: "You look thoughtful tonight!" Darnay said, putting his arm around her.
ko: "오늘 밤 생각에 잠긴 것 같군요!" 다네이가 그녀에게 팔을 두르며 말했다.

raw: “Yes, dearest Charles,” with her hands on his breast, and the inquiring and attentive expression fixed upon him; “we are rather thoughtful to-night, for we have something on our mind to-night.”
en: "Yes, dearest Charles," she said, placing her hands on his chest and looking at him closely. "I am rather thoughtful tonight, because I have something on my mind."
ko: "네, 가장 사랑하는 찰스." 그녀가 그의 가슴에 손을 얹고 그를 유심히 바라보며 말했다. "마음에 걸리는 것이 있어서 오늘 밤은 꽤 생각에 잠겨 있습니다."

raw: “What is it, my Lucie?”
en: "What is it, my Lucie?"
ko: "무엇인가요, 나의 루시?"

raw: “Will you promise not to press one question on me, if I beg you not to ask it?”
en: "Will you promise not to ask me why, if I beg you not to ask?"
ko: "만약 제가 묻지 말아 달라고 간청한다면, 이유를 묻지 않겠다고 약속해 주시겠어요?"

raw: “Will I promise?
en: "Will I promise?
ko: "약속하겠냐고요?

raw: What will I not promise to my Love?”
en: What wouldn't I promise to my love?"
ko: 나의 사랑에게 내가 약속하지 못할 것이 무엇이 있겠습니까?"

raw: What, indeed, with his hand putting aside the golden hair from the cheek, and his other hand against the heart that beat for him!
en: He pushed her golden hair back from her cheek, holding her close.
ko: 그는 그녀를 가까이 안으며 그녀의 뺨에서 금발 머리를 뒤로 넘겨주었다.

raw: “I think, Charles, poor Mr.
en: "I think, Charles, that poor Mr.
ko: "찰스, 제 생각에는 불쌍한 미스터

raw: Carton deserves more consideration and respect than you expressed for him to-night.”
en: Carton deserves more respect and consideration than you showed for him tonight."
ko: 카턴은 당신이 오늘 밤 그에게 보여준 것보다 더 많은 존중과 배려를 받을 자격이 있어요."

raw: “Indeed, my own?
en: "Really, my love?
ko: "정말인가요, 내 사랑?

raw: Why so?”
en: Why so?"
ko: 왜 그렇죠?"

raw: “That is what you are not to ask me.
en: "That is what you must not ask me.
ko: "그것이 바로 당신이 제게 묻지 말아야 할 것입니다.

raw: But I think--I know--he does.”
en: But I think, I know, he does."
ko: 하지만 제 생각에, 전 알아요, 그는 그럴 자격이 있어요."

raw: “If you know it, it is enough.
en: "If you know it, that is enough.
ko: "당신이 그것을 안다면, 그것으로 충분합니다.

raw: What would you have me do, my Life?”
en: What do you want me to do, my life?"
ko: 내가 어떻게 하기를 원하시나요, 나의 생명?"

raw: “I would ask you, dearest, to be very generous with him always, and very lenient on his faults when he is not by.
en: "I ask you, dearest, to always be very generous with him, and very lenient about his faults when he is not here.
ko: "사랑하는 이여, 그가 여기에 없을 때 항상 그에게 매우 관대하고 그의 허물에 대해 매우 너그럽게 대해 주시기를 부탁드려요.

raw: I would ask you to believe that he has a heart he very, very seldom reveals, and that there are deep wounds in it.
en: I want you to believe that he has a heart he rarely reveals, and that there are deep wounds in it.
ko: 저는 당신이 그가 좀처럼 드러내지 않는 마음을 가지고 있고, 그 안에 깊은 상처가 있다는 것을 믿어주시기를 원합니다.

raw: My dear, I have seen it bleeding.”
en: Dearest, I have seen his heart bleeding."
ko: 가장 사랑하는 이여, 저는 그의 마음이 피 흘리는 것을 보았어요."

raw: “It is a painful reflection to me,” said Charles Darnay, quite astounded, “that I should have done him any wrong.
en: Charles Darnay said in surprise, "It makes me sad to think I have wronged him.
ko: 찰스 다네이가 놀라서 말했다. "내가 그를 부당하게 대했다고 생각하니 슬퍼집니다.

raw: I never thought this of him.”
en: I never thought this of him."
ko: 나는 그에 대해 이런 생각을 해본 적이 없습니다."

raw: “My husband, it is so.
en: "My husband, it is true.
ko: "남편, 그것은 사실이에요.

raw: I fear he is not to be reclaimed; there is scarcely a hope that anything in his character or fortunes is reparable now.
en: I fear he cannot be reformed; there is little hope for his character or future.
ko: 저는 그가 교화될 수 없을까 봐 두려워요. 그의 성격이나 미래에 대한 희망은 거의 없어요.

raw: But, I am sure that he is capable of good things, gentle things, even magnanimous things.”
en: But I am sure he is capable of good, gentle, and noble things."
ko: 하지만 저는 그가 선하고 온화하며 고귀한 일들을 할 능력이 있다고 확신해요."

raw: She looked so beautiful in the purity of her faith in this lost man, that her husband could have looked at her as she was for hours.
en: She looked so beautiful in her faith in this lost man that her husband could have stared at her for hours.
ko: 이 길 잃은 사람에 대한 그녀의 믿음 속에서 그녀는 너무나 아름다워 보여서, 그녀의 남편은 몇 시간 동안이라도 그녀를 응시할 수 있었을 것이다.

raw: “And, O my dearest Love!” she urged, clinging nearer to him, laying her head upon his breast, and raising her eyes to his, “remember how strong we are in our happiness, and how weak he is in his misery!”
en: "And, oh my dearest love!" she urged, clinging closer to him and looking into his eyes. "Remember how happy and strong we are, and how weak he is in his misery!"
ko: "그리고, 오 나의 가장 사랑하는 사랑!" 그녀가 그에게 더 가까이 매달려 그의 눈을 들여다보며 간청했다. "우리가 얼마나 행복하고 강한지, 그리고 그가 그의 비참함 속에서 얼마나 약한지 기억해주세요!"

raw: The supplication touched him home. “I will always remember it, dear Heart!
en: Her plea touched his heart. "I will always remember it, my love!
ko: 그녀의 간청이 그의 마음을 움직였다. "항상 기억하겠습니다, 내 사랑!

raw: I will remember it as long as I live.”
en: I will remember it as long as I live."
ko: 제가 살아있는 한 그것을 기억할 것입니다."

raw: He bent over the golden head, and put the rosy lips to his, and folded her in his arms.
en: He bent over her, kissing her lips and holding her in his arms.
ko: 그는 그녀 위로 몸을 굽혀 그녀의 입술에 키스하고 그녀를 안았다.

raw: If one forlorn wanderer then pacing the dark streets, could have heard her innocent disclosure, and could have seen the drops of pity kissed away by her husband from the soft blue eyes so loving of that husband, he might have cried to the night--and the words would not have parted from his lips for the first time--
en: If the lonely wanderer walking the dark streets outside could have heard her words and seen her husband kiss away her tears of pity, he might have cried out to the night:
ko: 만약 밖의 어두운 거리를 걷는 외로운 방랑자가 그녀의 말을 듣고 남편이 키스로 그녀의 연민의 눈물을 닦아주는 것을 볼 수 있었다면, 그는 밤을 향해 이렇게 외쳤을지도 모른다:

raw: “God bless her for her sweet compassion!”
en: "God bless her for her sweet compassion!"
ko: "그녀의 달콤한 연민을 위해 하나님께서 그녀를 축복하시기를!"
